findings.title: Cancellation can leave the private terminal screen visible
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: The ordinary screen exit clears its active flag before terminal output completes and outside the drawing guard. The cancellation handler sees the flag clear and can exit before the terminal receives the screen-clearing sequence.
findings.impact: A handled cancellation can leave typed mnemonic words or other private output visible in the foreground terminal. Ordinary interactive input with redirected stdout can use a private screen independently of Flow. No disclosure was observed at runtime.
findings.recommendedFix: Serialize screen entry, physical teardown and cancellation with one guard. Keep a guard-aware helper for cancellation to preserve lock ordering.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Unix terminal restoration waits for output to drain
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: Both ordinary and signal cleanup restore terminal settings with TCSAFLUSH, whose contract waits for pending terminal output.
findings.impact: With device or driver output flow stopped, echo and mode restoration and handled cancellation can remain pending. The clean source does not establish the behavior of any particular real terminal during a stop.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the audited SPC restore semantics: discard pending input and restore immediately, preserving retry and error policy. Check the restore operation on Linux and macOS.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: The browser can terminate a worker before its final secret wipe
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: The worker queues its terminal reply before its finally block wipes transferred buffers. The page immediately terminates the worker when it receives that reply.
findings.impact: The browser may interrupt the worker at successful or rejected completion before its owned request arrays are wiped. The finding concerns early cleanup, with no demonstrated readback.
findings.recommendedFix: Wipe the request before sending either terminal reply. Keep immediate cancellation behavior and document its independently limited cleanup.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Missing-word search retains unzeroized copies of container indices
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: ContainerSearch owns typed container indices in an ordinary Vec. Producing a candidate clones the Vec, and words_of builds an ordinary vector of ordered word references before joining them.
findings.impact: Controlled intermediate copies of protected container data can remain in freed heap memory. The input here is an encrypted container and the audit establishes no direct mnemonic or password exposure.
findings.recommendedFix: Use zeroizing storage from parsing through candidate reconstruction and build the output without an unprotected intermediate vector of word references.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Windows redirected input can construct a File from an invalid handle
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: A failed GetConsoleMode test always reaches File::from_raw_handle. GetStdHandle can return NULL or INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE as an error sentinel.
findings.impact: The unsafe precondition requiring an open handle is violated when standard input is absent or acquisition fails. ManuallyDrop only suppresses closure, and no runtime corruption was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate both sentinels and return a controlled EOF or I/O error before constructing a wrapper. Verify the no-handle and valid redirected-input cases on Windows.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Cancellation can omit the warning for an unverified container
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: The unchecked-container flag is set after rendering. It is also cleared before reporting verification failure.
findings.impact: A handled cancellation in either interval can emit the generic cancellation text after a user has already seen an unverified container. The user may rely on a copy whose check never passed.
findings.recommendedFix: Publish the unchecked state under the drawing guard before writing any unchecked words. Clear it after validation succeeds or after the failed-check warning is visible.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.

findings.observed: The no-length callback uses the general reference parser, which accepts a wallet-check reference. Its TypeScript and guide allow an address, fingerprint or no reference.
findings.impact: The runtime accepts behavior hidden from typed callers. The 16-bit check remains a hint and does not confer authority to seal a rekey.
findings.recommendedFix: Constrain the callback to its documented variants or document and type the additional behavior explicitly.

findings.impact: A caller reusing the directory can receive checksums for old archives outside the selected package set. The Docker canonical job used a fresh directory and its six files were verified.

findings.title: The HTTP fuzzer can discard guaranteed complete request heads
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: An early return on parse errors handles arbitrary bytes and short complete generated heads alike. CI's fuzz input limit and the structured cases also stay below the 16 KiB head boundary.
findings.impact: A reader that starts rejecting every structured example can make the new routing assertions run on none of them. A separate unit test covers the cutoff.

findings.title: The Linux isolation fixture forks inside a multithreaded test harness
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: With Rust 1.99.1 a single test thread controls libtest concurrency while the harness main thread waits on the test worker. The fork child calls ordinary startup code and inspects a descriptor represented by a File still owned in the child after startup closes it.
findings.impact: The test can block on inherited state or violate file-handle assumptions. The defect affects evidence from the fixture, with no production fork identified here.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a dedicated, genuinely single-threaded subprocess fixture and transfer ownership of the descriptor before the code that closes it. Keep the reordered assertions.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: Loopback server copies an entire page into each accepted response
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: Rust clones the page into each accepted GET and HEAD response, then copies it again to serialize GET. Python concatenates a separate full GET response.
findings.impact: A valid selected page and simultaneous local requests can keep multiple page-sized buffers active. Availability impact is bounded to the loopback server and its configured limits.
findings.recommendedFix: Write headers and the shared page buffer separately under the existing per-connection deadline. HEAD needs only body length.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: A password repair from a different review can panic or select the wrong word
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: The public typed_word method slices the receiving review using the byte range carried by a public Repair value. The receiving review does not establish that the range belongs to its own text.
findings.impact: Combining reviews in a Rust caller can give a different word or panic on bounds or a UTF-8 boundary. Current CLI and WASM callers use their own review entries.
findings.recommendedFix: Take a position resolved within the receiving review and return a typed outcome. Retain correct same-review text for the native and browser callers.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the corrected invariant on the relevant target using public fixtures and retain the exact revision.

findings.title: The split Rust rekey API does not bind confirmation to its originating container
findings.reproduction: Static review of the exact committed code. No runtime vulnerability reproduction was performed.
findings.expected: The corresponding isolation, API, test or release boundary preserves its stated contract.
findings.observed: Rekey represents one container, but the public split methods accept recovery and confirmation values made by any Rekey session. Seal uses the supplied phrase with the receiving session's suite and old-password comparison.
findings.impact: A caller managing several backups can accidentally seal another independently confirmed wallet while applying the receiving session's metadata. No cross-session mixing was found in the shipped CLI or browser operation.
findings.recommendedFix: Bind recovery and confirmation to their originating Rekey and refuse mismatches before comparison or sealing. Preserve retry and length selection within one session.

reviewNotes: Tag release notes are transported separately from the canonical archive allowlist. Extending their digest binding is optional hardening under the current trusted-workflow model.

The retained MHFE Core audit records the Reed–Solomon 0.2.0 temporary value without explicit wipe and the SPC allocation-refusal limitation. Both exact dependency versions remain selected here. No new platform-wide claim about physical copies or recovery from allocation abort follows.
The previously documented path-restart limitation and deferred hidden-input fuzzer are tracked in AUD-049; no new ID is assigned to either.

The first local compare of archive digests used an excerpt filter that omitted the runner's digest lines. The retained names and digests come from the corrected comparison against the original CI log excerpt and the downloaded files.

remediation.evidence: Both named writers now use DRAWING. The password-heading regression passes on exact CI and scroll releases the lock before waiting for input. Cancellation during private screen teardown remains an independent blocker in AUD-051-SEC001.

Source recheck of attestation, draft and macOS/browser job inputs shows exact archive names and bytes bound to the canonical manifest. All six candidate archive hashes match the canonical runner log. The tagged attest and draft jobs remain unverified.
The exact hosted run passes a_search_of_two_root_shapes_describes_each. Both root shapes and input orders are exercised. The source counts address-type, program and root combinations.

The exact hosted run passes a_stop_ends_the_search_of_one_path_too. The path-specific branch checks stop before deriving the address key. The guarantee is at address derivation granularity, after constructing the master key.

The exact Chrome and Firefox standard and fast runs reject overlong strings, wider encodings and ordinary Uint8Array inputs. A subclass can shadow length while the native typed-array copy uses the intrinsic length. The original bounded-copy contract remains partly open.

The response oracle now independently checks headers, exact Host and expected GET/HEAD bodies. A source trace verifies the new predicates. The structured reader-rejection gap is tracked separately as AUD-051-ARC001; no exact five-minute CI fuzz run was available.

Both reordered assertions precede the memory-refusal acceptance branch. The parent fixture reports success in host and canonical CI, with child outputs suppressed. AUD-051-ARC002 qualifies that evidence because the harness still forks from a libtest worker.
TARGETS names four fuzz targets and DEVELOPMENT describes the registry pin and both checksum-locked manifests. Reconciled with the active files.

limitations: This is ordinary V2 with pre-tag source and candidate evidence. Full release-profile host suites, full-cost vectors, full-size browser checks, distribution launchers and tagged distribution execution are separate evidence.

No exact compatible Miri run, sustained hosted fuzz campaign or corpus coverage receipt was available. The local fuzz cap is 30 seconds per run. No heavy local run was admitted at the observed thermal threshold.
Branch CI does not exercise the attestation or draft jobs from release.yml. No signed release tag, tag-only runtime on canonical distribution files, attestation or publication was checked.
One canonical Docker build was verified against six artifacts. No independent second canonical rebuild was performed. Hosted macOS does not establish a task-port refusal with SIP enabled.

This review classified all tracked paths and inspected unchanged operational boundaries. Per-line coverage of every active file, re-execution of historical harnesses and review of all dependency internals were not established.
New findings are static. No vulnerability reproduction, disclosure experiment or proof of secret extraction was performed.
